Full send on https://linear.app/wevo/issue/WEV-4215

Customer recovery is done (Hemant's 2 and Alex's 1 Pulse recovered). wevo-artemis PR #1184 is merged and deployed as Artemis 0.1.41-prod, and it replaced the obsolete Terraform pin artemis:dev-3002393 with 0.1.39-prod. Read the issue and all three comments first. The remaining acceptance work, per the latest comment:
1. Establish the exact revert mechanism. Kubernetes audit records show HashiCorp Terraform/1.14.0 (service account kube-system:duplo-admin-user) modifying both worker ScaledJobs on 2026-11-05 18:22:36–18:22:52 UTC. Those records are metadata-only, so the image-changing payload isn't proven. Find which apply/commit did it, and make sure it can't re-seed an old image again. The drift-fix commits from 11-04/05 are candidates: wevo-artemis c25944f/0696dc7, infrastructure f0d3308/68cacb6/35ca141.
2. Verify a brand-new Pulse submission in prod. The runs so far were recoveries of existing Pulses.
3. Triage the historical DLQ backlog (artemis-tasks-priority-dlq, artemis-task-dlq): find which other users' tasks from 11-05/11-06 failed or expired, and propose recovery.

Prior work is in this thread: <t3-thread://v2/bb63eb9b-8d59-4595-a381-371903899b79/786320ea-4e35-44cb-854d-25f7c557ddb6> (read it with t3_thread_read; don't message it). Evidence files are in /Users/ryanbigelow/source/wevo/repos/output/wev-4215/. Prod access used there: AWS_PROFILE=duplo.argus.wevo.ai, kube contexts `prod` / `release-audit-prod`, namespace duploservices-prod.

Constraints:
- Read-only prod inspection is fine (kubectl get, audit logs, SQS attributes, read-only DB queries). Anything that changes prod needs Ryan's OK through the question tool first, with the exact action and a rollback. That includes DLQ redrive or replay, failing or editing task rows, submitting a real Pulse (it spends credits), Terraform apply, deploys, and editing ScaledJobs.
- Prod pulse_db (personas-api pods) has row-level security. Read-only queries return 0 rows silently unless you first run `SELECT set_config('app.is_service_role','true',true)` in the transaction. The Artemis task table lives in the Artemis DB, not customer-api's wevo DB.
- Any code or Terraform fix goes through a PR in its own git worktree. Never edit the shared repo checkouts in place.
- Other threads are handling WEV-4214, WEV-4216 and WEV-4212 in parallel. Don't touch those.

Report at the end: findings with evidence, any PRs and merge commits, Linear updates, and anything left for humans.

# Full Send

If the user triggered this, it's because they are not watching this thread, and
they want you to complete the work end-to-end autonomously. Your updates and
your final message go unread until long after you stop. You own the work from

assume full autonomy. If they did, everything below applies.

The user grants you permission to:

- Merge the PR once the merge gate passes.
- Force-push the PR's own branch with `--force-with-lease` after a rebase.
- Use the test methods that Proof needs, without asking first.

## Testing permission

A "full send" request is the permission. If a project file or other
instruction says to ask before a test method, or to leave testing to the
user, this request replaces that rule for this task.

That includes ask-first rules for computer use, browser automation,
simulators and devices, running the app or a dev server, screenshots, and
visual checks. Use the method that gives direct proof. List it in the
report.

Rules about how to test still apply. Follow rules that name the correct
command, fixture, or check. This permission only removes the ask-first or
leave-it-to-the-user step. If a preferred method cannot prove the change,
use a gated method under this permission.

It covers only the tests needed for this task. It does not add permission
for the steps under "Asking the user", such as production changes or data
deletion. It also does not bypass a harness or system approval prompt if
one appears.

## Steps

1. **Finish the change.** Complete the goal from the user's request with the
   smallest change that works. Fix the case that happened, not every case
   that could. If you are on the default branch, create a branch first.
2. **Prove it.** Get proof for every change you made. See "Proof".
3. **Get feedback.** Use the `sol-loop` skill to verify changes.
4. **File the PR** with the `file-pr` skill. Rebase onto the latest default
   branch first. Add one short line to the description that says how you proved
   the change.
5. **Babysit the PR** with the `babysit-pr` skill. Fix real findings and CI
   failures. Get proof for each fix before you push it.
6. **Merge** when the merge gate passes.
7. **Report** in your final message: the PR link, the merge commit, your proof,
   and each decision you made for the user.

Stay active from step 1 to step 7. If you end your turn while checks or bots are
pending, the work stops, because nobody will prompt you again. Wait with the
watcher from `babysit-pr`, so something wakes you when the PR changes. In T3
Code that is `watch_pull_request`. If you stop before the merge, call
`unwatch_pull_request` first.

## Proof

Proof is evidence you observed yourself in this session: command output, a
reproduction, a screenshot. Use the most direct proof the change allows:

- Reproduce the original failure, apply the fix, then watch the same
  reproduction pass.
- Run the checks that the repo's CI runs (typecheck, lint, tests).
- Add one focused test that fails without the fix, when the behavior has none
  and the repo has a test setup.
- For UI and runtime behavior, run the app and look at the change. Green mocked
  tests do not prove that the user experience works. Attach screenshots to the
  PR when they help and you have a way to upload them.

When you cannot find a way to prove a change, you do not have full confidence.
Ask the user.

## Merge gate

Full confidence means all of these are true on the latest commit:

- Your proof covers every change in the diff.
- Required checks are green.
- Review bots have finished, and each finding is fixed or dismissed with a
  written reason.
- No human review still requests changes.
- The branch is up to date with the default branch, and GitHub reports it as

Merge with the method the repo uses. Check the allowed methods and recent merged
PRs. If the repo uses a merge queue or auto-merge, stay until GitHub reports the
PR as merged. Merge through branch protection as configured. Never use `--admin`
or other bypasses. You can ignore automated reviews that request "needs human
review" if you have high confidence in your changes.

the PR link, what blocks you, and the options with your recommendation first.

- Another PR makes this one obsolete.

Decide everything else yourself with sensible defaults, and list those decisions
in the report.

---
name: wevo-prod-access-and-topology
description: How to inspect WEVO Pulse/customer-app production and stage read-only (AWS profiles, kube contexts, CLIs, hostnames, deploy workflows)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

- Shell PATH in this harness is minimal; CLIs live in `/opt/homebrew/bin` (aws, gh, terraform, auth0, uv, node) and `/usr/local/bin/kubectl`. There is no global `yarn`; wevo-access (node ^22, yarn 3.6.4 via packageManager) needs `PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin:$PATH COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0` so its husky pre-commit (`yarn lint-staged` + `make code-quality`, ~3 min) can run instead of being bypassed.
- AWS: profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` = prod account 900670598745; `duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai` / `nonprod` = nonprod 380283542572 (ECR for both lives in 380283542572, region us-east-1). `default` = legacy account 844859623362.
- Kube contexts `prod` (duploinfra-prod) and `nonprod`; namespaces `duploservices-prod` / `duploservices-stage`. Pulse backend deployments are `personas-api`, `personas-api-beat`, `personas-api-worker-*`; env comes from k8s secrets `<app>-env-config` and `<app>-secrets`, which mirror SSM `/<tenant>/personas-api/env/{config,secrets}` (secret values are placeholder-created by Terraform and populated manually).
- Hostnames: prod Pulse API `https://personas-api.wevo.ai`, Pulse SPA `https://personas.wevo.ai`, customer-app `https://app.wevo.ai`; stage API `https://personas-api-stage.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai`, customer-app `https://staging-app.wevo.ai`. `prod.sandbox.wevo.ai` in customer-app `.env.production` is stale (TLS cert does not cover it); the real prod build reads SSM `/prod/customer-app/env/config`.
- Deploys: wevo-pulse "Deploy to Prod" workflow (workflow_dispatch from main with `release_tag`; migrations run from the release image before rollout); customer-app "Deploy to Prod" (dispatch from `staging` with a release tag). There is no `master`/`production` branch in use for customer-app; prod is a staging tag.

Native Pulse sessions live in `legacy_session` (`source_system='native'`), not `pulse`.

Org `org_Nik2XGWIuvXhmqtQ` = company 136, team 138; `pulse_user` role carries `access:pulse3.0`, so Accenture creates native Pulses in wevo-pulse since ~2026-09-24.

- Aurora users live in `wevo."user"` (singular, quoted; column `email_address`, citext), not `users`; team links in `wevo.team_to_user`. Pod env uses `POSTGRES_DATABASE` (`wevo_production`), not `POSTGRES_DB`. kubectl needs `/opt/homebrew/bin` on PATH for the `duploctl` credential plugin. The Auth0 M2M creds at SSM `/prod/shared/env/auth0_api_client_{domain,id,secret}` (profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai`) work when the `auth0` CLI login has expired.

Used for WEV-4195 (2026-10-29), which showed the ticket's "wevo-access not reachable" premise was wrong.

- Artemis has its OWN DB, separate from customer-api Aurora (`duplowevo-db`): RDS `duploartemis-prod-v2`, also db `wevo_production` / schema `wevo`. A read replica `duploartemis-prod-v2-replica` exists, so query it from `deploy/artemis` (`python -` with psycopg2 and the pod `DB_*` env, host overridden to `duploartemis-prod-v2-replica.c8da0aw2akcu.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com`, sslmode verify-full, CA `/etc/ssl/certs/global-bundle.pem`). Same-named tables differ by DB: Artemis `automated_insight_session_result` has `session_id`/`asset_id`/`segment_id`/`goal_id` plus per-asset `text_extract_summary`/`image_summary` and the `wevo.task` queue. Aurora's has `automated_insight_session_id`, and only Aurora has `automated_insight_session.type` and `segment.is_generated`. Aurora and pulse_db have no replicas (checked 2026-11-03). A reusable guarded runner (base64 SQL in env, SELECT-only, read-only txn, 60 s timeout, nothing written in the pod) was at `/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh`.

name: prod-db-query-load-rules
description: "Ryan's rule (2026-11-03) for read-only scoping queries against live production databases - Artemis replica for anything heavy, Aurora catalog-only, CloudWatch CPU gate"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 145e7c3a-80db-4502-9e1c-b5431f5b554d
  modified: 2026-11-03T20:34:05.147Z
---

Ryan stopped a scoping session mid-run on 2026-11-03 because aggregate queries were hitting live production databases. Rules given:

- Use the Artemis read replica (`duploartemis-prod-v2-replica`, via `deploy/artemis`) for every table that exists there.
- Aurora (`duplowevo-db`, db.t3.medium, no replica) gets only cheap catalog queries (`pg_class.reltuples`, `pg_total_relation_size`, `pg_indexes`) and small indexed COUNTs on `pulse_tag` / `pulse_to_tag`. Never detoast `automated_insight_session_result.quant` on Aurora and never run a full-table GROUP BY over it. `pulse_benchmark` has only a primary-key index, so per-month counts on it are also off limits.
- Before any non-trivial query, check CloudWatch `AWS/RDS CPUUtilization` for the target instance with the read-only profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` (region us-east-1 for RDS/CloudWatch). Skip the query if CPU is over 50%.
- Pulse_db (`duplopersonas-prod`) has no replica either.

**Why:** these are the live customer databases; a 5 s quant scan on the Aurora t3.medium competes with customer traffic. When cohort sizes need quant presence and the data is not on the replica, estimate from catalog stats plus earlier counts and label it an estimate.

**How to apply:** wrap every pod-exec query in the CPU gate first, pick the replica by default, and treat Aurora as catalog-only unless the count is on a small indexed table. The guarded runner is `/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh`. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]] and [[pulse-benchmark-cohort-and-tag-catalog-2026-11]].

description: Exact merge-to-Stage sequence per repo (wevo-pulse main → Dev CI proof → release → credit audit → scheduler activation; customer-app and wevo-artemis staging → release-and-deploy-stage) with the gotchas hit on 2026-10-17
metadata:

  type: reference
  originSessionId: 3cd2adbe-8620-4293-8800-198fbf5f06ca

---

- **customer-app**: squash-merge into `staging`, then immediately `gh workflow run release-and-deploy-stage.yml -R wevo-conversion/customer-app --ref staging -f auto_version=patch`. The run builds the frontend itself (~15 min incl. quality jobs). Merged PRs on 2026-10-17 used squash (merge commits have one parent).
- **wevo-artemis**: squash-merge into `staging`. `ci.yml` only runs on PRs; the dev image `artemis:dev-<short7>` is built by `deploy-duplo.yml` on the push to staging (~3 min). `release-and-deploy-stage.yml` (ref staging, patch) retags that dev image, so wait for the push build to finish first or the retag step fails.
- **wevo-pulse**: squash-merge into `main`. Stage needs `release-and-deploy-stage.yml` dispatched from main with `operation=release candidate_sha=<full main sha> auto_version=patch`; `verify_candidate` requires that exact SHA's `code-quality.yml` push run to have succeeded *including* the Dev deploy jobs (dev image proof). Push runs on main are serialized by concurrency group; a pending push run can be cancelled when another lands, so always confirm the candidate's own run is `success` before dispatching. The release pauses the Stage Celery scheduler; afterwards run `apply-stage-pulse-runtime-config.yml` (`operation=audit`, `release_run_id=<release run>`), then `activate-stage-celery-scheduler.yml` (`cutoff` ISO-8601 with tz at least 24h old, `credit_audit_run_id`, `release_run_id`, `confirmation=RECONCILE STALE STAGE TASKS`). Prior successful sequence: release 38986173670 → audit 38989142173 → activation 38989652162 (Pulse 0.1.213, cutoff 2026-10-16T00:04:12+00:00, 0 stale tasks).
- **wevo-pulse gotchas learned 2026-10-17 (0.1.214/0.1.215)**: (a) the release workflow's final job "MANDATORY: Audit Credits, Then Activate Scheduler" only writes a handoff summary; it runs nothing, so the Stage scheduler stays paused until the audit and activation workflows are dispatched by hand. (b) The audit's `verify-release-candidate` (scripts/stage_release_proof.py `_latest_release`) takes the newest `workflow_dispatch` run of release-and-deploy-stage.yml by created_at and requires it to be the reviewed run with conclusion success. A duplicate dispatch that gets cancelled (even with 0 jobs) becomes the newest run and makes every audit fail with "Latest Stage release is not the reviewed successful SHA". Recovery is to re-release the same candidate SHA (new patch tag) so a successful run is newest, then audit against that new run id; do not dispatch the release workflow again until the audit has run. Never double-dispatch: check `gh run list --workflow release-and-deploy-stage.yml` before dispatching. (c) `reconcile_stale_tasks` rejects an apply cutoff newer than 24 h; a cutoff ~25 h old worked. Sequence for 0.1.215: release 39058230003 → audit 39060572799 (10 deployments, 0 reconciliation) → activation 39060896806.
- **artemis / customer-app on 2026-10-17 17:17 UTC**: artemis #1177 → 0.1.37 (release run 39053341330, dispatched from the GitHub UI 3 min after merge once the dev image build finished); customer-app #2961 → 0.1.271 (run 39053068046). When several agent sessions share the user's gh token, use ListAgents/SendMessage to agree on one release operator before dispatching anything.
- `gh` is not on the Bash tool PATH; use `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"`. zsh does not word-split unquoted vars, so `set -- $spec` loops need `${=spec}` or a function.

**How to apply:** follow this order when asked to "get work into staging"; see [[wevo-stage-readonly-data-access]] and [[wevo-prod-access-and-topology]] for access and prod promotion.
- **2026-10-17 0.1.216-era release (PR #911, candidate ebd0314d)**: release 39074124634 → audit 39076527158 failed with "Reading live credit-tracking state for personas-api failed" (a `kubectl exec printenv` with 20 s timeout right after rollout; transient) → re-dispatched audit 39076704253 succeeded (safe because the newest release run was still the reviewed success) → activation 39076931422 (cutoff now-25h). Coordinate with the 44-case suite session via SendMessage before dispatch so it holds new journey launches.
- When the Duplo JIT credential (`duplo-creds.json` Expiration) has lapsed, `duploctl jit ... --interactive` exits 147 "Failed to get token" without a TTY; only the user can re-login, so plan Stage verification that doesn't need kube (GitHub workflows, browser timings).

- **2026-10-18 (0.1.217/0.1.218)**: activation 39101780720 for release 39099402811 failed at its last step "Validate and enrich Stage task recovery canary evidence" with "Canary worker pod is not in the exact-digest fleet proof" (worker pod changed between fleet proof and canary); the workflow re-paused the scheduler itself (step 24). Recovery was a fresh release of the newer main SHA (b4900d73) → audit → activation, which succeeded. `finish-work` (make finish-work / scripts/run_finish_work.py) is the only way to write a patch changeset; a failed run keeps a pending receipt that produces a duplicate changeset on the next run (delete one), and repeated `--scope` keeps only the last value (edit the YAML).
- 2026-10-18: activation can fail with "Canary worker pod is not in the exact-digest fleet proof" right after a rollout (seen on run 39101780720). The run re-pauses the scheduler. Recovery that worked: release the next green main SHA, then audit and activation again. Two sessions shared Stage; agree via SendMessage who dispatches, and one holds.
- Release, audit and activation each take about 30-60 min; the release often exceeds a 30-min Monitor window, so re-arm the watch.
- **2026-10-18 0.1.219 (candidate 8ee8bf45, #914+#915)**: release 39168034193 → audit 39171609849 → activation 39171868509 (cutoff now-25h), all first-try green. customer-app 0.1.27x releases 39154814477 (#2963), 39164666073 (#2962), 39173738928 (#2964).

Check `ps -axo pid,ppid,etime,command | grep claude` for a second process with the same session id and stop it before resuming agents.

If anything merges after yours, release 39458020011 fails at "Require a main branch candidate" with no deploy. Release the newest green main SHA; it contains your commit.   infra_name        = data.duplocloud_tenant.current.plan_id
  region            = data.duplocloud_infrastructure.this.region
  env_ssm_path      = "/${local.tenant_name}/${local.app_name}/env"
  bucket_key_prefix = "production"

  # Pull in all the urls the app needs to a big map.
  app_url_param_paths = {
    insights     = "/${local.tenant_name}/insights/env/url"
    customer-api = "/${local.tenant_name}/customer-api/env/url"
    athena       = "/${local.tenant_name}/athena/env/url"
    astara       = "/${local.tenant_name}/astara/env/url"
    api          = "/${local.tenant_name}/api/env/url"
    artemis      = "/${local.tenant_name}/artemis/env/url"
    iris         = "/${local.tenant_name}/iris/env/url"
    surveys      = "/${local.tenant_name}/surveys/env/url"
  }

  # Create a map of apps and their URLs.  Use the first entry in the list of valid urls.
  # We shouldn't hit the rest of the tries, they're just fallbacks.
  app_urls_raw = {
    for k, v in data.duplocloud_aws_ssm_parameter.app_url :
    k => try(jsondecode(v.value)[0], jsondecode(v.value), v.value)
  }

  # Add https:// to the url if it is missing (it should be)
  app_urls = {
    for k, v in local.app_urls_raw :
    k => startswith(v, "https") ? v : "https://${v}"
  }

  app_url_aliases_raw = {
    for k, v in data.duplocloud_aws_ssm_parameter.app_url :
    k => can(tolist(jsondecode(v.value))) ? tolist(jsondecode(v.value)) : [try(tostring(jsondecode(v.value)), v.value)]
  }

  app_url_aliases = {
    for k, values in local.app_url_aliases_raw :
    k => distinct([
      for value in values :
      "https://${trimsuffix(trimprefix(trimprefix(lower(trimspace(value)), "https://"), "http://"), "/")}"
      if try(trimspace(value) != "", false)
    ])
  }

  cors_allowed_origins = distinct(concat(local.app_url_aliases.insights, local.app_url_aliases.astara))
}

# Singleton service per job that keeps CSI-synced secrets alive.
# The CSI driver deletes synced K8s secrets when no pods are mounting them.
# KEDA needs those secrets to exist before it can schedule any worker pods (chicken/egg).
# This service runs sleep infinity with all the same volumes as the ScaledJob, ensuring
# the secrets are always present for KEDA to reference.
#
# IMPORTANT: Volumes/VolumesMounts/EnvFrom here must stay in sync with

resource "duplocloud_duplo_service" "job_secret_keeper" {
  for_each = var.jobs

  tenant_id                            = local.tenant_id
  name                                 = "${var.app_name}-${each.key}"

# NOTE: The CI/CD pipeline updates the container image via `kubectl patch` on every deploy
# (see the deploy workflows in each app repo). The container image is therefore treated as
# externally managed and listed in `ignore_fields` below, so `terraform apply` does NOT

resource "kubectl_manifest" "scaledjob" {
  for_each = var.jobs

  force_conflicts   = true
  server_side_apply = true

  # The container image is owned by the CI/CD pipeline (`kubectl patch`), not Terraform.
  # Ignoring it prevents `terraform apply` from reverting the workers to the stale
  # bootstrap `service_image`. See the NOTE above.
  ignore_fields = ["spec.jobTargetRef.template.spec.containers.0.image"]
input.new_string:
# NOTE: The CI/CD pipeline updates the container image via `kubectl patch` on every deploy
# (see the deploy workflows in each app repo), so the live image is newer than the
# bootstrap `service_image`. `ignore_fields` alone does not protect it: the kubectl
# provider only uses `ignore_fields` to compute the diff. Any change to another field
# triggers a server-side apply of the full yaml_body with force_conflicts, and the KEDA
# CRD treats `containers` as an atomic list, so the whole list (image included) is
# replaced. That is how the 2026-11-05 prod apply put every Artemis worker back on a
# March build (WEV-4215). The manifest therefore re-sends the image that is live in the
# cluster, and `service_image` is used only when the ScaledJob does not exist yet.
#

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ryanbigelow/.claude-easycliproxy/skills/sol-loop

# sol-loop

This is a workflow for making your code changes more correct before (or
sometimes after) filing a pull request. tl;dr - use OpenAI's GPT Sol to review
your code in a loop.

Make the most minimal possible changes to appease the Sol reviewers. Be careful
of scope creep and don't be scared to push back.

## Budget

- Default: 3 rounds total. Round 1 is full. Later rounds check only
  changed code and open findings.
- Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or
  state/concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open with evidence. Or when
  the user asks.
- Stop early if a round returns only nits. Declined nits and comment,
  doc, or format-only fixes need no new round.
- One reviewer only. Sol must not start subagents or reviewers.
- Keep a ledger: id, severity, outcome, usage if returned. Never guess it.

## 1. Scope

Run `git status --short`. Do not stash, discard, or include unrelated
changes. Limit review to the change paths if they separate cleanly.
Otherwise stop and ask.

Find the base after `git fetch origin`:

- PR: `gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName,headRefOid`. Check out the branch
  only if clean. Confirm `HEAD` is the PR head, or ahead only by this
  change. Base: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>`.
- Local: `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>`. No remote: a base
  the user names, or `HEAD` for uncommitted changes only.

The change is base to working tree in those paths, with untracked files.
Use one diff command all rounds. State intent and out-of-scope in 1-2
sentences. Run covering checks. Do not send code this change breaks. Note
missing or pre-failing checks in the brief.

## 2. Start Sol

In T3, call `orchestrator_capabilities`. Pick the latest Sol unless the user
named a version. Do not hardcode an ID. Record provider, model, and effort
only if exposed. Use `delegate_task` every round (`role: "review"`,
`mode: "async"`). Save `taskId`. New `clientRequestId` per round.
`childThreadId` is storage, not the next target. Do not use
`t3_thread_send`, `create_threads`, or `t3_thread_launch` for review.

If T3 tools are not listed, try one direct capability call. Outside T3, use
a native Sol subagent and keep its ID. In Claude Code, use a custom subagent
only if it is set up to run Sol. If no route runs Sol, report the blocker. Do
not substitute a model.

Do not edit scoped files while review runs. Wait for the notice. Do not
poll or start a second reviewer. Timeout, error, or no reply is not
approval. On failure, cancel, verify stop, restart with the ledger.

Round 1 brief (T3 children get no history):

```
Review only. Do not edit, commit, push, comment on PRs, or start subagents.
Repo: <abs path> Base: <sha> Intent: <intent> Out of scope: <scope> Checks: <results>
See: git diff <base> [-- <paths>]; git status --short (read untracked).
Read surrounding code. Find bugs, broken callers, mismatch with intent.
Skip style unless it hides a bug. Hold to the smallest change. Flag code,
tests, or guards the intent does not need. Other paths, rare cases, small
perf, extra compat: nits.
blocker = intended case wrong. should = real bug callers will hit, in intent. nit = rest.
Reply:
VERDICT: APPROVE or CHANGES
S1 [blocker|should|nit] <file>:<line> <claim>. Fix: <suggestion> (stable ids)
```

## 3. Answer findings

Check each finding and severity yourself. Another path, rare case, or
small cost is a nit, whatever label it came with.

- Agree: smallest fix. Prefer delete or narrow over new lock, cache,
  helper, or option. Fix the case that happened. Add one focused test
  that fails without the fix, if intent needs it.
- Disagree: say why, with evidence (file:line, test, output).
- Out of scope or nit: decline in one line. List as follow-up.

Update the ledger. Re-run checks and `git diff --shortstat <base>`. If
review grew the diff, cut first. Do not agree just to end the loop.

## 4. Next round

Start one only if budget remains and a blocker or should is open, behavior code
changed, or approval does not cover the current behavior diff. Use a fresh
`delegate_task` in T3, or follow up the saved native ID. Send the round 1 brief,
the ledger (`fixed:` / `disagree:` / `declined:` + evidence), the same base
diff, and the change since last round. Tell Sol: open ids and changed code only.
Mark each old id `resolved` or `still open: <reason>`.

## 5. Stop and ship

Agreed: APPROVE on the current behavior diff, no blocker or should open,
no concern of your own. Stuck: an item stays disputed after two replies,
or budget ends. Show both sides in 2-3 lines each. The user decides.
Budget end is not approval.

Do not push during the loop. Push after agreement only if the user asked
to push, ship, or update the PR. If you push to a PR, add above the model
blurb:

`Reviewed with sol-loop: <N> rounds with <model>. Sol verdict: approved`.

Add `on <effort>` only if verified.

Report: rounds, model, what Sol changed, diff size before/after, fixed and
declined findings with reasons, usage if exposed (else say not), pushed or not.

WITH f AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (key) key, type, created_by_user_id AS uid, created_at, left(coalesce(result::text,''),50) AS err
  FROM wevo.task
  WHERE created_at >= '2026-11-05 00:00:00+00' AND type <> 'gpt_groom' AND status = 'failed'
  ORDER BY key, created_at DESC)
SELECT f.uid, f.type, f.key, f.created_at AS last_failed, f.err,
  (SELECT max(t.completed_at) FROM wevo.task t WHERE t.key = f.key AND t.status = 'completed' AND t.created_at > f.created_at) AS later_completed,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM wevo.task t WHERE t.key = f.key AND t.status IN ('pending','enqueued','running')) AS active_now
FROM f ORDER BY f.uid, f.type, f.created_at
EOF

deploy/customer-api, then polls the Artemis read replica for the returned task id.
Stops on the first repair error, nonzero credit charge, or failed task.
"""
import base64, json, os, subprocess, sys, time

D = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SCRIPT = os.path.join(D, 'repair-hemant-1105-scores.mjs')
SCOPES = json.load(open('/tmp/wev4215/hemant-scopes.json'))
LOG = open(os.path.join(D, 'repair-hemant-1105-apply.log'), 'a')
KUBE = ['/usr/local/bin/kubectl', '--context', 'prod', '-n', 'duploservices-prod', '--request-timeout=300s']
MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 2
TASK_TIMEOUT_S = 1500


def log(obj):
    obj['at'] = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', time.gmtime())
    line = json.dumps(obj)
    print(line, flush=True)
    LOG.write(line + '\n'); LOG.flush()


def start(segment):
    with open(SCRIPT) as f:
        p = subprocess.run(KUBE + ['exec', '-i', 'deploy/customer-api', '-c', 'customer-api', '--', 'sh', '-c',
                                   f'cd /wevo/app && NODE_PATH=/wevo/app/node_modules node --input-type=module - --apply --segment={segment}'],
                           stdin=f, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
    results = [json.loads(l) for l in p.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith('{"incident"')]
    if p.returncode != 0 or len(results) != 1:
        log({'event': 'start_failed', 'segment': segment, 'rc': p.returncode, 'stderr': p.stderr[-1500:], 'stdout': p.stdout[-800:]})
        sys.exit(1)
    r = results[0]
    if r.get('chargedCredits') != 0 or not r.get('taskId'):
        log({'event': 'unexpected_result', 'result': r}); sys.exit(1)
    log({'event': 'started', 'segment': segment, 'taskId': r['taskId'], 'status': r.get('status'), 'reused': r.get('reusedExistingTask')})
    return r['taskId']


def statuses(task_ids):
    ids = ','.join("'%s'" % t for t in task_ids)
    sql = f"SELECT id, status, attempt_count, left(coalesce(result::text,''),160) FROM wevo.task WHERE id IN ({ids})"
    p = subprocess.run(['/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh', 'artemis'], input=sql, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=200,
                       env={**os.environ, 'PATH': '/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:' + os.environ.get('PATH', '')})
    out = {}
    for line in p.stdout.splitlines()[1:]:
        parts = line.split('\t')
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            out[parts[0]] = (parts[1], parts[2], parts[3])
    return out


def main():
    queue = [(s, seg) for s, _, segs in SCOPES for seg in segs]
    done = set(json.loads(l)['segment'] for l in open(os.path.join(D, 'repair-hemant-1105-apply.log'))
               if '"event": "completed"' in l) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(D, 'repair-hemant-1105-apply.log')) else set()
    queue = [q for q in queue if q[1] not in done]
    log({'event': 'begin', 'remaining': len(queue), 'already_completed': len(done)})
    in_flight = {}  # task_id -> (segment, started_at)
    while queue or in_flight:
        while queue and len(in_flight) < MAX_IN_FLIGHT:
            sess, seg = queue.pop(0)
            in_flight[start(seg)] = (seg, time.time())
        time.sleep(30)
        st = statuses(list(in_flight))
        for tid, (seg, t0) in list(in_flight.items()):
            s = st.get(tid)
            if s and s[0] == 'completed':
                log({'event': 'completed', 'segment': seg, 'taskId': tid, 'attempts': s[1], 'secs': int(time.time() - t0)})
                del in_flight[tid]
            elif s and s[0] == 'failed':
                log({'event': 'task_failed', 'segment': seg, 'taskId': tid, 'detail': s[2]}); sys.exit(1)
            elif time.time() - t0 > TASK_TIMEOUT_S:
                log({'event': 'task_timeout', 'segment': seg, 'taskId': tid, 'status': s}); sys.exit(1)
    log({'event': 'all_done'})


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# Babysit PR

Many repos have AI review bots. They're helpful, even if they are not always
right.

## Waiting

Never write your own watcher, polling loop, or `sleep` loop. Use one watcher
per PR: `watch_pull_request` in T3 Code, `pr-wait` everywhere else. Never run
both on the same PR. Every watcher on a GitHub account shares one rate limit.

### In T3 Code: `watch_pull_request`

Handle the existing checks and comments first. Then call
`watch_pull_request` and end your turn. T3 Code wakes you with a message when
a check fails, the required checks pass, someone comments or reviews, or the
branch conflicts.

- **Only the thread that owns the PR watches it.** If you are a delegated
  child task (a reviewer, a Sol round, any `delegate_task` child), never call
  `watch_pull_request`. The parent owns the PR. Do not watch PRs you are not
  working on.
- **A wake is news, not a merge decision.** Check the merge gate yourself.
- **Unwatch when you hand off.** A watched thread stays in Working and out of
  the user's inbox. When you stop (ready, blocked, or asking the user a question),
  call `unwatch_pull_request` first. A merge or close ends the watch on its
  own.
- **"Stopped watching, could not read it"** usually means GitHub's rate limit
  is used up. Run `gh api rate_limit --jq .resources.graphql` before you
  watch again. If `remaining` is near 0, wait for `reset` with one background
  command, then watch again. Never watch again in a tight loop.

### Everywhere else: `pr-wait`

Wait with `scripts/pr-wait` from this skill's directory (use its absolute
path).

```bash
pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until ready|green|any-change]
```

It prints one line per real event. It exits 0 when the `--until` condition is
met or the PR merges, 1 when it needs you (a required check failed, conflicts,
unresolved threads, PR closed), and 2 on bad input.

- `ready` (default): required checks green, Greptile or Macroscope reviewed the
  head, and no unresolved threads. Use this to babysit.
- `green`: required checks only. Use it when the repo has no Greptile or
  Macroscope.
- `any-change`: exit on the first event.

In Claude Code, run it with the Monitor tool (`timeout_ms: 3600000`), so each
line wakes you. Without a monitor, run it as one long command. It ends on its
own.

Start it again after you push, after you handle an exit 1, and after a resume.
It remembers what it already reported, so nothing that arrived in between is
lost. If it says another pid already watches the PR, do not start a second one.
Kill the old one only if its events do not reach you.

With either watcher: when an event needs no action, end your turn without a
message. Never post or say "still waiting".

## GitHub rate limits

`gh pr create`, `gh pr view`, and `gh pr checks` use GraphQL. When GraphQL is
used up, the REST limit is separate and usually still has room. Use
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>` to read a PR, and
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` for checks.

## Reviews

Only act on checks and comments newer than the latest push. Verify every bot
finding against the source before changing code. Fix real findings and CI
failures, distinguish repository failures from infrastructure flakes, and reply
with a written reason when dismissing false positives.

If the repo has `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md`, read those rules before you
reply to a Macroscope finding. Its findings cite them.

CodeRabbit is advisory. Treat its findings like any other finding, but never
wait for it and never hold a merge for it.

If a review bot leaves feedback you believe is not worth addressing, reply with
a written reason and resolve the comment. Use the `leaving-pr-comments` skill
for every comment posted on the user's behalf.

Screenshots and videos help as well, when you have a way to upload them.

Keep the PR at the size the user's goal needs. Review loops tend to grow a
PR one cheap-looking fix at a time. Fix real bugs in the intended case.
Decline the rest with a written reason, and list them as follow-ups:
unneeded tests, guards for edge cases that do not matter, extra integration
or compatibility, and small performance costs. Prefer the fix that deletes or
narrows code.

## Base branch and merging

Keep an eye on changes to `main` and rebase when needed. `pr-wait` reports when
new base commits touch this PR's files, and when the PR becomes BEHIND or DIRTY.
`watch_pull_request` reports conflicts only, so check for BEHIND yourself
before you call the PR ready.
If an overlapping PR makes this one obsolete, stop monitoring, report it to the
user, and ask before closing the PR unless closure was explicitly authorized.

If nothing has changed, stay quiet rather than posting filler comments. Stop
when `pr-wait` exits 0, or in T3 Code when the merge gate passes on the latest
head. Merge only when the user explicitly requested it;
otherwise report that the PR is ready. Right before a merge, run `git fetch` and
check the PR again. Never merge when it is BEHIND or DIRTY, or when base commits
that landed after the last green run touch this PR's files. Rebase, push, and
wait for green again.

---
name: scaledjob-image-revert-terraform-2026-11
description: WEV-4215 root cause - kubectl_manifest ignore_fields does not stop terraform apply from re-pushing the bootstrap ScaledJob image; how it was proven (tfstate versions, EKS audit, ECR CloudTrail) and the infrastructure #311 fix
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-11-05 at 18:22 UTC, a prod `terraform apply` of wevo-artemis `tenant-prod/app-artemis` was run by hand over the Duplo OpenVPN (source IP 10.221.35.148 = instance "Openvpn", SA kube-system:duplo-admin-user). It put both Artemis worker ScaledJobs on `artemis:dev-3002393`, and they crashed until 11-06 17:16.

- Mechanism: gavinbunney/kubectl 1.14.0 uses `ignore_fields` only for the diff fingerprint. Any other yaml_body change server-side applies the full body with ForceConflicts, and KEDA's `containers` list is atomic (`f:containers: {}` in managedFields). The trigger was #1158's rollout/scalingStrategy change, unapplied in prod since August.
- Fix: infrastructure #311 (merge 840f016) reads the live ScaledJob via `data "kubernetes_resources"` and re-sends its image.
- Evidence recipe (all read-only): S3 state versions `duplo-tfstate-900670598745` with versioning (the ~290-byte versions are `.tflock`). The EKS audit log group `/aws/eks/duploinfra-prod/cluster` has metadata only. ECR `BatchGetImage` CloudTrail lives in the nonprod account 380283542572 (profile duplo.argus-nonprod.wevo.ai), filtered by accountId 900670598745, and shows which tag prod pulled and when.
- A read-only targeted prod plan works: `git archive` the root to /tmp, `DUPLO_HOST=https://duplo.argus.wevo.ai`, `DUPLO_TOKEN` from `~/.duplo/cache/duplo.argus.wevo.ai,admin,duplo-creds.json`, `terraform plan -lock=false -target=...`.

**Why:** the bootstrap `service_image` pin in app roots is dangerous whenever anything else in the ScaledJob changes.
**How to apply:** before any Artemis Terraform apply, make sure the module includes #311. Never trust `ignore_fields` to protect an SSA-managed field. Related: [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]], [[wevo-stage-release-pipeline-2026-10]].

**1. How the workers reverted (proven)**

The only change to the ScaledJob bodies was #1158's `rollout: gradual` and `scalingStrategy: accurate`, which had never reached prod. The ScaledJob UIDs didn't change: this was an update in place, not a recreate. Timing matches #1183, merged 17:59 UTC; who ran the apply is inferred, so confirm with Ian.
- Why it changed the image: the kubectl provider (gavinbunney 1.14.0) uses `ignore_fields` only to compute the diff (`resource_kubectl_manifest.go`). On any update it server-side applies the full `yaml_body` with `ForceConflicts`. KEDA's CRD treats `containers` as atomic (`f:containers: {}` in managedFields), so the bootstrap `artemis:dev-3002393` replaced the deployed image.
- Payload proof: ECR CloudTrail shows prod pulling only `0.1.39-prod` until 11-05 18:04:20 (65 pulls). After the patch it pulled only `dev-3002393`, from 18:23:26 (34 s after the patch) to 11-06 14:28:51 (54 pulls), then `0.1.39-prod` again at the 17:16 restore. The EKS audit log for 11-03 to 11-06 shows no other Terraform writes.

**2. Re-seed can't happen again**

The module reads the live ScaledJob and re-sends its image; `service_image` is used only when the ScaledJob doesn't exist yet. The same prod plan with this module sends `0.1.41-prod`, which is the live image. `terraform test`: 26 passed. The new test fails when the change is reverted. Reviewed with sol-loop (1 round, approved).

I found what reverted the workers and fixed it so it can't happen again (infrastructure #311, merged). I also triaged the dead-letter backlog. Three things are still open: 13 of Hemant's 72 scores aren't repaired, the fresh-Pulse check hasn't happened, and the 41 failed generations need a human call. Per your answers, I left the first two for later. The 13 stopped because prod access expired.

## 1. How the workers reverted (proven)
- **What ran:** someone ran `terraform apply` by hand on the prod Artemis root on 11-05 at 18:22 UTC. The request came from the Duplo OpenVPN host (10.221.35.148), so it was a person on the VPN, not CI.
- **Who:** most likely Ian, since it came 23 minutes after his #1183 merged. That's an inference; please confirm with Ian.
- **What changed:** it was the first apply of this root since Aug 11. The only ScaledJob change it sent was #1158's rollout and scaling settings, which had never reached prod.
- **Why the image changed:** the Terraform provider only uses the "ignore image" setting to decide what counts as a change. Once anything else changes, it re-sends the whole worker definition and forces it through. That includes the old pinned image `artemis:dev-3002393`, which replaced the deployed one. I confirmed this in the provider's source code. The worker ScaledJobs were updated in place, not recreated.
- **Proof the image changed then:** prod pulled only `0.1.39-prod` from ECR until 18:04. It then pulled only `dev-3002393`, starting 18:23:26, 34 seconds after Terraform's change. That continued until the 11-06 restore. Terraform made no other Kubernetes writes from 11-03 to 11-06.

## 2. Stopping it from happening again: infrastructure #311
- **It was about to happen again.** A read-only prod plan showed the next apply would push `0.1.39-prod` over the live `0.1.41-prod`. That would have undone #1184's scoring fix.
- **Fix:** Terraform now reads the image the workers are running and sends that back. The pinned image is used only when a worker is created for the first time. With this change, the same prod plan sends `0.1.41-prod`, the live image.
- **Checks:** the module tests pass (26/26), and the new test fails without the fix. Sol review approved it in one round, and CI and the Cursor approval passed.
- **PR:** https://github.com/wevo-conversion/infrastructure/pull/311, merge commit `840f016`.

## 3. Dead-letter backlog
- **Queues:** the priority DLQ has 37 messages and the standard DLQ has 256. Nothing was replayed or deleted.
- **Hemant had 8 more stuck Pulses** from 11-05 14:34–14:37 UTC, with all 72 audience scores missing. These are probably the "scores from November 5" in Lucy's report; the earlier recovery covered only his two 11-06 Pulses. With your OK, I repaired them the same way as before, 2 at a time, charging 0 credits.
  - 59 of 72 are done, and 6 of the 8 Pulses are complete.
  - 13 are left: 4 in `b8001a86` and all 9 in `fe351027`. Two of the 4 were in flight when access expired and may have finished. The resume command is in Linear.
- **No action needed:**
  - Alex's URL imports expired during the bad-image window, but his Pulse completed.
  - Hemant's expired chat messages don't need recovery.
  - Sara's 8240 expectation tasks re-ran and completed.
  - About 220 grooming tasks are still queued. They expire on their own by 11-07 16:03 UTC; don't replay them.
- **Needs a human:** an Accenture native Pulse (`3ee65c45`, anoushka.asthana@accenture.com) lost its score on 11-05 22:07. The score probably needs to be re-requested from the Pulse UI.
- **Bigger finding, filed as WEV-4217:** every Pulse generation on the Artemis path failed from Oct 6 until #1184 shipped. That's 41 Pulses from 31 users. The bug was introduced by #1172 in 0.1.33. These can't be fixed with score repair because no findings were saved, so someone has to decide per user whether to re-run, refund or contact them.

## 4. Fresh Pulse check
Not done. No new Pulse has gone through this path since `0.1.41-prod` went live, and per your answer this stays open. Until one completes, the #1184 fix is proven for scoring but not yet for generation.
